audience.programmeDescription: WUR’s Dutch-taught Molecular Life Sciences programme studies how molecules and cells function through chemistry, biology and physics, with a strong chemistry focus. Experimental research connects molecular mechanisms to medicines, materials and other applications.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The first UCR programme combines molecular biology and biochemistry with chemical applications and mathematical/computational methods. The second puts more weight on disease and drug-action research. WUR provides substantially more organic and physical chemistry, quantum/atomic theory, synthesis, spectroscopy and specialist laboratory work. Its 21-credit experimental thesis is required; UCR’s optional independent research is additional to the illustrated 180 credits.

componentNotes.bml-choice: Three-credit choice determined by prior mathematics. This example is for Mathematics A preparation and takes Mathematics Applied: Introduction before Analysis and Linear Algebra. Students with Mathematics B take Statistics 1 instead.
componentNotes.bml-thesis: Required 21-credit experimental research project, with a reproducible laboratory journal, report, presentation and final discussion. Entry requires at least 102 prescribed credits including all 60 first-year credits and 42 second-year compulsory credits, plus the supervising group’s introductory second-year preparation. This example completes all prescribed taught study first and uses Biochemistry after both second-year BIC courses.
componentNotes.bml-electives: Thirty-six open credits remain for a minor and/or individual electives. No particular minor, internship or specialist package is assumed.
componentNotes.bml-responsibility: Includes debate about a molecular-science controversy, reflection on the scientist’s role, visits to at least two potential employers and an ethics portfolio. All portfolio reports must be sufficient to complete this 3-credit course.
componentNotes.bml-practical-gene-protein: Compulsory molecular laboratory study, including DNA/RNA/protein analysis, cloning, PCR, enzyme activity and bioinformatics. General and laboratory safety are additional zero-credit requirements.
componentNotes.bml-protein-biochem: Combines biocatalysis with a full-time protein-purification practical. The theory assessments and combined practical/lab-journal result each require a passing grade; laboratory safety is required.

Shared waves, optics, Fourier analysis and material/physical reasoning address an identifiable part of the physics foundation; WUR additionally develops classical mechanics and electromagnetism for later quantum/atomic study.

Shared chemical equilibria, complexation, adsorption and thermodynamic process analysis address environmental/water applications of chemical driving forces. WUR adds a more extensive mathematical thermodynamics and kinetics treatment.
